I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. The type check shows no errors for it, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 636 bytes (min+gzip) with 95 bytes of your own code. I did not run the original or the migrated functions on sample inputs, so equal results are not tested.

I could not get a baseline size or type-check result for `src/module.ts`. Its size run crashed, and `tsc` reports the lodash modules as not found, so lodash isn't installed. The only type errors `tsc` reported were in `src/module.ts`.

I checked the installed es-toolkit (version 1.53.2) before choosing functions:

- **`mapValues`:** the main `es-toolkit` entry has it, and it keeps the same keys and maps each value, so `doubled` is unchanged.
- **`keyBy`:** the main entry has it, and the last element wins for duplicate keys, like lodash. It takes only a function, not the `'name'` shorthand, so I used `(row) => row.name`, which is the only adapter in the file.
- **`isEmpty`:** only `es-toolkit/compat` exports it. I read its source: it returns `true` for null, numbers and booleans, and checks length for strings and arrays. It returns whether an object has no own keys, as lodash does, so `isBlank` is unchanged for your input range.

No lodash import remains, and I didn't hand-write any replacements for the utilities.
